blocks.name: immediate_gen
blocks.responsibility: Generate sign-extended I, S, B, and J immediates and the zero-extended U immediate from the instruction word.
blocks.design_rationale: Centralizing immediate extraction reduces duplicated logic and makes the split B- and J-immediate mappings straightforward to verify.

blocks.name: register_file
blocks.responsibility: Provide two asynchronous register reads and one synchronous write for the 32 RV32 registers; enforce x0 as zero and clear register state during asynchronous active-high reset.
blocks.design_rationale: An isolated register file makes x0 and reset behavior independently verifiable while retaining the two-read, one-write structure needed for single-cycle execution.

blocks.name: alu
blocks.responsibility: Implement RV32I arithmetic, logic, shifts, and signed and unsigned comparisons, plus all RV32M multiply, divide, and remainder operations, selected by opcode, funct3, and funct7.
blocks.design_rationale: Keeping operation decoding and arithmetic in one combinational block limits top-level datapath complexity and allows the complete RV32IM operation set to be tested in isolation.

blocks.name: control_unit
blocks.responsibility: Decode the instruction opcode and funct3 to produce register-write, memory-write, load, memory-width, signed-load, ALU operand-source, writeback-source, branch, and jump controls.
blocks.design_rationale: Separating instruction control from datapath calculations makes memory side effects, writeback selection, and control-flow decisions easier to inspect and validate.

blocks.name: cpu
blocks.responsibility: Implement the specified single-cycle RV32IM top level: maintain the PC, instantiate the generated datapath and control blocks, select and extend load data, drive store and instruction buses, and commit PC and register updates on the rising clock edge.
blocks.design_rationale: The top-level owns only architectural sequencing and bus integration, preserving the exact external contract while allowing its constituent logic to be verified independently.

notes: The ALU operands are selected by the CPU for register, immediate, or PC-relative operations. The CPU performs branch comparisons using the register operands and instruction funct3, and selects load bytes or halfwords using the effective address low bits.
